newsitem.title: USA: Kimberly-Clark saves more than $250 mln.
newsitem.headline: Kimberly-Clark saves more than $250 mln.

text.p: Kimberly-Clark Corp said Tuesday it moved aggressively in 1996 to integrate its operations with those of Scott Paper Co, realizing savings in excess of its target of $250 million.

The $9.4 billion merger between Kimberly-Clark and Scott Paper Co closed in December of 1995. The cost savings included personnel reductions and consolidation of manufacturing facilities, said Kimberly-Clark Vice President of Corporate Communications Tina Barry in a telephone interview.
"There are also synergies in distribution and advertising," Barry said.

Continued strong performance in Kimberly-Clark's personal care businesses and the benefits of the merger drove the company's 1996 earnings and overcame the impact of lower selling prices for the company's U.S. consumer and international tissue products and for newsprint, the company said.
